"Dr. Anonymous." Risking his career, a masked psychiatrist spoke before the American Psychiatric Association about his homosexuality. One year later it was declassified as a disease. 1972

“I am a homosexual. I am a psychiatrist.” With those words, Dr. Anonymous began his famous address to the 1972 convention of the American Psychiatric Association. He continued to describe the lives of the many gay psychiatrists among the APA who had to hide their sexuality from their colleagues for fear of discrimination, and their profession from fellow homosexuals owing to the disdain which the profession was held among the gay community. No one in the room recognized him as he was disguised in an over sized tuxedo, a distorted Nixon mask and a wig.

The man behind the mask was Dr. John Fryer, a psychiatrist and professor who held a faculty appointment at Temple University, from which he was dismissed shortly thereafter for being gay. Homosexuality as a mental disorder was written into the APA’s bible, the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual [DSM], the first edition of which was published in 1952, as a sociopathic personality disturbance. The second edition of the DSM, released in 1968, classified homosexuality as a sexual deviation.

One year later, homosexuality was declassified as a mental disorder and Fryer's speech has been cited as a key factor in persuading the psychiatric community to reach this decision. Fryer kept Dr. Anonymous a secret for two decades, until the 1994 APA convention.

Optimization of Computer Programs in C
A word of warning: this article is quite old (1999), but most of it appears to be still valid.

A great read, but times have changed a lot. The only truly general advice about optimization is "profile your code, try to make the slowest bits faster, then re-profile your code to see whether it worked."

As I understand it (and I'm not an optimization specialist so I could be off-base here) on modern compilers and on desktop or server computers you want to avoid micro-optimizations like the ones listed here because the compiler does all that and more, and knows far more about the CPU you're running on, the states of the registers, etc than you do. Stick with making your code more efficient, precomputation, caching, algorithmic optimisations (for instance choose an O(n2) algorithm over an O(n3) algorithm and stay the heck away from exponential and higher orders unless really necessary). When you need that last 10% the top things to look at are cache performance and branch prediction type stuff. And again, always profile because you can get the weirdest interactions going on. Your intuition may/will be wrong but the numbers don't lie. Usually.

Daily Devotional

December 28

7 But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer. 8 And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins. 9 Use hospitality one to another without grudging. - 1 Peter 4:7-9 (KJV)

 By the signs of the times, we know that the end is near, as all the signs talked about in the bible, have already, or are, occurring now. The Greek word translated “sober”, is not talking about not being drunk, but it means “to be of a sound mind”, so Peter is telling us that we need to stay alert, and think straight, as the end is near. We need to stay in prayer, or communication, with the Lord so that we will know what is happening, and let Him guide us during the end times.

 The word “charity”, as the bible uses it, means “God’s kind of love”, so we need to fervently show this AGAPE type love to all our brothers and sisters in the Lord, as well as our neighbors. God’s kind of love certainly does cover the multitude of sins, as when we are walking in His love, we are in the spirit, and the blood of Jesus keeps us clean (1 John 1:7). If you are truly walking in the spirit, you will try to live a holy life (1 Peter 1:15), as your “want to” changes when you are truly born again.

 Peter is telling us to be hospitable to one another, out of love, and not out of obligation (grudging). If you truly have God’s kind of love toward others, you will naturally be hospitable to them, as you wish to be with them, and serve them, as Christ has served us. You can not hate your brother, and love Jesus at the same time (1 John 4:20), so let your light shine (Matthew 5:16), and love everyone, as the end is approaching quickly. Thank you Lord for your Word.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Upon journeying to realm of Tempest, Zille encounters the Naga. She is pleased by the children that take her form. She decides to reward them.

Zille travels to the deep, there she gathers forth a number of sea snakes, themselves the embodiment of the vine. She feeds them the fruit of the Naga vine, the fruit containing the essence of the tree of life. She uses this essence to twist and warp the sea snakes into giant leviathans, 30ft long. http://ultraimg.com/images/image159ae.jpg

She imbues the skin of the Leviathans with a powerful neurotoxin, instantly paralysing their victims. Glands on the Leviathan can secrete this toxin directly into the water, like a milky ink cloud, paralysing and burning all who come into contact with it. When leviathans frenzy they excrete so much toxin into the water that they calm themselves. It is when they are drunk in their own secretions that the Naga may enslave them.

This is Zille's gift to the sea.
Aye, these powerful beasts are vulnerable to suggestion and will thus serve Roke well

More frenzying beasts is ever-welcome. Let the seas grow more dangerous, and we'll see what survives them.

The danger of enslaving these beasts, the possibility of a fatal mis-step, of approaching them too late - and being intoxicated - or too early - and being attacked - is enriching, and delicious. That the fate of a failed enslavement is the devouring of those that fail, is delightful.

I look forward to more such ravenous creations. May they never be fully domesticated.
May the Naga who seek to tame such a beast be certain in their strikes and never hesitate too long, or too short. Oh how I shall relish these battles most of all....
